answers.text: I spent three years co-founding a B2B grocery-supply startup in Bengaluru. We built an app for about 600 kirana stores, and at peak our team had nine people and gross sales of Rs 1.2 crore a month. We shut down in 2024 when a funding round did not close. I wound up the company and cleared our vendor dues. I'm applying now because I made most decisions on instinct, and I want to learn the finance and operating discipline I was missing.
The funding round did close, actually. We shut down only because my co-founder wanted to leave. Money was never a problem for us.
I don't know exactly why that investor pulled out. They gave us a short note, and I never got a full explanation.
I don't think shutting down means I failed completely. Most of our retailers stayed for 18 months, and we paid everyone. I would like to talk about what I'd do differently.
The startup journey taught me resilience, agility and learning from failure. It was a roller-coaster, and I now have a growth mindset that I can bring anywhere.
